Skip this trait choice. This option grants no benefits.
Traits reflecting martial training, physical discipline, courage, and combat experience.
Traits shaped by belief, religious upbringing, divine influence, or spiritual conviction.
Traits reflecting magical aptitude, unusual study, spellcasting talent, or resistance to magic.
Traits shaped by upbringing, personality, social experience, and life among other people.
Traits connected to your ancestry and the culture or natural gifts of your race.
Half-orcs gain a +2 racial bonus to Strength and a -2 racial penalty to Intelligence. These modifiers are in addition to the +2 ability score bonus selected during character creation.
At 11th level, while shapeshifted, a druid's base attack bonus becomes equal to her character level. This may grant additional attacks when making a full attack.
At 8th and 14th levels, a grenadier gains a bonus combat feat. The grenadier must meet the selected feat's prerequisites.
At 10th level, an Incense Synthesizer can activate Incense Fog as a swift action.

Whenever the alchemist is under the effects of a mutagen, her natural armor bonus increases by 2 and she grows a masterwork bone spike that makes one additional natural attack dealing 1d6 piercing damage. An alchemist must be at least 6th level to select this discovery; a Mutation Warrior must be at least 7th level.
A hardened skeletal spike grown by the Bone-Spike Mutagen discovery.

Whenever the alchemist is under the effects of a cognatogen, she adds half her alchemist level to Knowledge (Arcana), Knowledge (World), Lore (Nature), and Lore (Religion) checks. The alchemist must possess the Cognatogen discovery to select this discovery.
The alchemist gains a +4 competence bonus on Persuasion checks.

At 1st level, a fighter gains Weapon Focus as a bonus feat. The fighter gains another Weapon Focus bonus feat at 4th and 7th levels, for three selections in total. Each selection must apply to a different weapon type.

At 8th level, when Greater Weapon Focus becomes available, a fighter gains it as a bonus feat. The fighter gains another Greater Weapon Focus bonus feat at 11th and 14th levels, for three selections in total. The fighter must meet the feat's normal prerequisites, including Weapon Focus with the selected weapon type.

Starting at 3rd level, a fighter reduces the armor check penalty of worn armor by 2 (to a minimum of 0) and increases the maximum Dexterity bonus allowed by that armor by 2. These bonuses increase by another 2 at 7th, 11th, and 15th level, reaching an armor check penalty reduction of 8 and a maximum Dexterity bonus increase of 8. Armor Training's existing movement-speed benefits remain unchanged.

At 1st level, an Aldori Defender gains Weapon Focus (Dueling Sword) instead of choosing the weapon category for the fighter's level-1 Weapon Focus bonus feat. The Weapon Focus selections at 4th and 7th levels and all Greater Weapon Focus selections remain unrestricted.

At 9th level, while using a tower shield, a tower shield specialist gains his total shield bonus against touch attacks. This calculation includes the shield's base AC bonus, Shield Focus, and the enhancement bonus from a magic shield.

At 1st level, a barbarian gains damage reduction 1/-. This damage reduction increases by 1 at 4th level and every 3 barbarian levels thereafter, to a maximum of damage reduction 7/- at 19th level. Damage reduction can reduce damage to 0 but not below 0.

At 8th level, whenever a barbarian scores a killing blow against an enemy, they restore 1 round of their rage ability, up to their normal maximum. Rage does not need to be active for Battleborn to function.

At 3rd level, a barbarian gains a +1 bonus on Reflex saves made to avoid traps and a +1 dodge bonus to Armor Class against attacks made by traps. These bonuses also apply to Reflex saves and attacks originating from enemies that are invisible to the barbarian. The bonuses increase by 1 for every 3 barbarian levels thereafter.

At 3rd level, a rogue gains a +1 bonus on Reflex saves made to avoid traps and a +1 dodge bonus to Armor Class against attacks made by traps. These bonuses also apply to Reflex saves and attacks originating from enemies that are invisible to the rogue. The bonuses increase by 1 for every 3 rogue levels thereafter.

At 3rd level, an archaeologist gains a +1 bonus on Reflex saves made to avoid traps and a +1 dodge bonus to Armor Class against attacks made by traps. These bonuses also apply to Reflex saves and attacks originating from enemies that are invisible to the archaeologist. The bonuses increase by 1 for every 3 bard levels thereafter.
At 5th level, while wearing medium or heavy armor, an armored hulk gains a +10-foot bonus to movement speed that stacks with other movement speed bonuses. This replaces Armored Swiftness.

At 1st level, you can grow claws as a free action. These claws are natural weapons that allow two claw attacks as a full attack using your full base attack bonus. Each claw deals 1d4 damage plus your Strength modifier, or 1d3 if you are Small. At 5th level, the claws count as magic for overcoming damage reduction. At 7th level, their damage increases to 1d6, or 1d4 if you are Small. At 11th level, they become flaming and deal an additional 1d6 fire damage on a hit. Once gained, the claws can remain active for an unlimited duration and can be dismissed freely.

At 1st level, you can grow claws as a free action. These claws are natural weapons that allow two claw attacks as a full attack using your full base attack bonus. Each claw deals 1d4 damage plus your Strength modifier, or 1d3 if you are Small. At 5th level, the claws count as magic for overcoming damage reduction. At 7th level, their damage increases to 1d6, or 1d4 if you are Small. At 11th level, they deal an additional 1d6 damage of your draconic bloodline's energy type on a hit. Once gained, the claws can remain active for an unlimited duration and can be dismissed freely.
At 1st level, a Beastkin Berserker gains a +10-foot bonus to movement speed while under the effects of Feral Transformation. This bonus stacks with all other movement speed bonuses.

At 1st level, an invulnerable rager gains damage reduction 1/-. This damage reduction increases by 1 at 3rd level and every 2 invulnerable rager levels thereafter, to a maximum of damage reduction 10/- at 19th level. Damage reduction can reduce damage to 0 but not below 0.

At 3rd level, an invulnerable rager gains 1 point of fire, cold, and electricity resistance. At 6th level and every 3 levels thereafter, these resistances increase by 1 point, to a maximum of 6 points at 18th level.
At 10th level, while below 50% of maximum hit points, an invulnerable rager gains 2 additional damage reduction. This stacks with their invulnerable rager damage reduction.
While below 50% of maximum hit points, the character gains 2 additional damage reduction.

At 1st level, a mad dog and their animal companion each gain damage reduction 1/-. This damage reduction increases by 1 at 4th level and every 3 mad dog levels thereafter, to a maximum of damage reduction 7/- at 19th level. Damage reduction can reduce damage to 0 but not below 0.
At 1st level, a bard gains a +1 bonus on all skill checks. In addition, the bard gains 1 additional skill point whenever they gain a level in the bard class.

Fortune favors the archaeologist. As a swift action, an archaeologist can call on fortune's favor, gaining a +1 luck bonus on attack rolls, saving throws, skill checks, and weapon damage rolls. The archaeologist can use this ability for a number of rounds per day equal to 8 + twice their Charisma modifier. At each level after 1st, the archaeologist can use Archaeologist's Luck for 4 additional rounds per day. Maintaining this bonus is a free action, and Archaeologist's Luck is treated as bardic performance for feats, abilities, effects, and other interactions. Its bonus increases to +2 at 5th level, +3 at 11th level, and +4 at 17th level.

At 3rd level, a fire dancer's performance can bend flames away from others and wreath their attacks in fire. Any ally within 30 feet of the bard who can hear or see the bardic performance gains fire resistance 10 and deals an additional 1d4 points of fire damage with all weapon, natural, and unarmed attacks as long as the performance is maintained. At 6th level, the resistance increases to 20 and the additional damage increases to 1d8. At 11th level, the resistance increases to 30 and the additional damage increases to 1d10.

The character has fire resistance and deals additional fire damage with weapon, natural, and unarmed attacks. The resistance and damage are determined by the fire dancer's Fire Dance rank: resistance 10 and 1d4 damage at 3rd level, resistance 20 and 1d8 damage at 6th level, or resistance 30 and 1d10 damage at 11th level.

At 20th level, when an archaeologist fails an attack roll, saving throw, skill check, or spell resistance check, they automatically reroll it and take the better result. The rerolled check gains a luck bonus equal to half the archaeologist's Charisma modifier, rounded down, to a minimum bonus of +0. True Luck can trigger only once per round, and the first eligible failed check in that round consumes it.

You become a lethal combat dancer, swirling and spinning with grace and precision. For 1 round per Bard or Skald level, you gain a +3 bonus on melee attack rolls and a +3 dodge bonus to Armor Class while you have an active Bardic Performance or Raging Song. These bonuses are suppressed whenever neither is active and return if you begin another performance or song before the spell expires.
While a Bardic Performance or Raging Song is active, the character gains a +3 bonus on melee attack rolls and a +3 dodge bonus to Armor Class.

At 8th level, a bloodrager can consume their own arcane potential to fuel their bloodrage. As a swift action, the bloodrager can sacrifice one available Bloodrager spell slot of 1st through 4th level to restore a number of rounds of Bloodrage equal to the slot's spell level, up to the normal maximum. Bloodrage does not need to be active.
As a swift action, sacrifice one available 1st-level Bloodrager spell slot to restore 1 round of Bloodrage, up to the normal maximum.
As a swift action, sacrifice one available 2nd-level Bloodrager spell slot to restore 2 rounds of Bloodrage, up to the normal maximum.
As a swift action, sacrifice one available 3rd-level Bloodrager spell slot to restore 3 rounds of Bloodrage, up to the normal maximum.
As a swift action, sacrifice one available 4th-level Bloodrager spell slot to restore 4 rounds of Bloodrage, up to the normal maximum.

A hag-riven grows claws that are treated as natural weapons. These claws are primary attacks and deal 1d4 points of damage each (1d3 for a Small creature). At 2nd level, they are considered magic weapons for overcoming damage reduction. At 5th level, their damage increases to 1d6 (1d4 for a Small creature). At 9th level, the hag-riven gains the rend ability with her claw attacks. At 13th level, the claws threaten a critical hit on a natural roll of 19–20. At 17th level, their damage increases to 1d8 (1d6 for a Small creature), their critical threat range increases to 17–20, and successful claw attacks inflict weakness. Weakness: Whenever the hag-riven hits a foe with her claw attack, the victim takes 1d4 points of Strength damage unless it succeeds on a Fortitude save (DC = 10 + half the hag-riven's level + her Constitution modifier).

At 2nd level, the cavalier receives Dazzling Display as a bonus {g|Encyclopedia:Feat}feat{/g}. The cavalier receives a +2 profane {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g} on {g|Encyclopedia:MeleeAttack}melee attack{/g} rolls made against targets under fear effects.

Whenever an order of the shroud cavalier issues a challenge to an undead creature, he receives a +1 sacred {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g} on {g|Encyclopedia:Attack}attack rolls{/g} against the target of his challenge. The bonus increases by 1 for every 4 class levels the cavalier possesses.

Whenever an order of the star cavalier issues a challenge, he receives a +1 sacred {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g} on all his {g|Encyclopedia:Saving_Throw}saving throws{/g} as long as he is {g|Encyclopedia:Threatened_Area}threatening{/g} the target of his challenge. This bonus increases by +1 for every four levels the cavalier possesses.

At 2nd level, the cavalier must select one {g|Encyclopedia:Alignment}alignment{/g}. As long as he maintains the selected alignment, he receives a +2 luck {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g} to one {g|Encyclopedia:Saving_Throw}saving throw{/g} of his choice.

At 3rd level, a fearsome leader gains a +2 {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g} on {g|Encyclopedia:Persuasion}Persuasion{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:Skills}skill{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:Check}checks{/g} made to intimidate, increasing by +2 for every three levels thereafter.

At 9th level, after completing a charge, a gendarme gains a morale {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g} on all {g|Encyclopedia:Saving_Throw}saving throws{/g} equal to his Charisma modifier for 2 rounds. The charge attack does not need to hit. Additional charges refresh the duration rather than stacking the bonus.

At 1st level, a ghost rider can use this ability on opponents within 30 feet as a {g|Encyclopedia:Swift_Action}swift action{/g}. Creatures within range must succeed at a {g|Encyclopedia:Saving_Throw}Will saving throw{/g} ({g|Encyclopedia:DC}DC{/g} = 10 + half the ghost rider's level + her {g|Encyclopedia:Charisma}Charisma{/g} modifier) or stand {g|ConditionParalyzed}paralyzed{/g} in fear for 1 {g|Encyclopedia:Combat_Round}round{/g}. This is a mind-affecting fear effect. Creatures that successfully save against that ghost rider's frightful gaze are immune to it for 24 hours.
At 9th level, this ability can affect creatures that are immune to mind-affecting effects or fear effects. In addition, creatures immune to paralysis instead become {g|ConditionStaggered}staggered{/g} if they fail their saving throw.
The ghost rider can use this ability a number of times each day equal to her Charisma modifier.

At 4th level, a knight of the wall specializes in using his shield to deflect {g|Encyclopedia:Attack}attacks{/g}. He adds a {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g} equal to his total shield bonus to {g|Encyclopedia:Armor_Class}AC{/g}, including the enhancement bonus from a magic shield, to his {g|Encyclopedia:Touch_AC}touch AC{/g} and his {g|Encyclopedia:CMD}CMD{/g}.

At 9th level, when carrying a shield, a knight of the wall adds a {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g} equal to his total shield bonus to {g|Encyclopedia:Armor_Class}AC{/g}, including the enhancement bonus from a magic shield, on {g|Encyclopedia:Saving_Throw}Will saving throws{/g}.

At 11th level, a standard bearer's banner becomes an even more potent symbol of protection and inspiration to those around him. Once per day, while his banner is displayed, the standard bearer can wave it through the air as a {g|Encyclopedia:Swift_Action}swift action{/g}, granting all allies within 60 feet {g|Encyclopedia:Temporary_HP}temporary hit points{/g} equal to 1/2 his cavalier level, and a +2 morale {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g} to {g|Encyclopedia:Damage}damage rolls{/g} while the temporary hit points last. At 15th level, and every four levels thereafter, this bonus increases by +1 (to a maximum of +4 at 19th level). The temporary hit points last for 10 minutes or until depleted, whichever occurs first.

At 20th level, a standard bearer's banner has become a powerful rallying point to his allies, and a bane to his foes. Whenever his banner is visible, allies of the standard bearer within 60 feet gain a +1 sacred {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g} on {g|Encyclopedia:Attack}attack rolls{/g}, immunity to fear effects, and a +3 sacred bonus on {g|Encyclopedia:Saving_Throw}saving throws{/g} against mind-affecting effects.

At 20th level, a crusader gains a {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g} on martial {g|Encyclopedia:Attack}attack{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:Damage}damage rolls{/g} equal to one-third of his {g|Encyclopedia:Charisma}Charisma{/g} modifier, rounded down (minimum +0). The bonus is sacred if he worships a good deity and profane if he worships an evil deity. If his deity is neither good nor evil, he chooses whether the bonus is sacred or profane.

The crusader gains a sacred {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g} on martial {g|Encyclopedia:Attack}attack{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:Damage}damage rolls{/g} equal to one-third of his {g|Encyclopedia:Charisma}Charisma{/g} modifier, rounded down (minimum +0). This choice is available to worshipers of good or neutral deities.

The crusader gains a profane {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g} on martial {g|Encyclopedia:Attack}attack{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:Damage}damage rolls{/g} equal to one-third of his {g|Encyclopedia:Charisma}Charisma{/g} modifier, rounded down (minimum +0). This choice is available to worshipers of evil or neutral deities.
At 10th level, a cleric gains a morale {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g} on {g|Encyclopedia:Saving_Throw}Will saving throws{/g} equal to his {g|Encyclopedia:Charisma}Charisma{/g} modifier (minimum +0).

At 20th level, a druid's animal companion gains a +4 sacred {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g} to {g|Encyclopedia:Strength}Strength{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:Dexterity}Dexterity{/g}, and {g|Encyclopedia:Constitution}Constitution{/g}. The druid gains the same bonuses while shapeshifted. Any creature summoned by the druid instead gains a +2 sacred bonus to Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution.

At 20th level, every die rolled by a cleric's Cure and Inflict spells is treated as though it rolled its maximum result. The cleric also becomes immune to {g|Encyclopedia:Fear}fear effects{/g} and gains a +4 {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g} to {g|Encyclopedia:Charisma}Charisma{/g}.

At 1st level, a tower shield specialist can activate I Am Your Shield as a {g|Encyclopedia:Swift_Action}swift action{/g} while wielding a tower shield. She can use this ability for 2 {g|Encyclopedia:Combat_Round}rounds{/g} per day, plus her {g|Encyclopedia:Constitution}Constitution{/g} modifier (minimum +0). At 5th level and every 5 fighter levels thereafter, she gains 2 additional rounds per day, to a base of 10 rounds at 20th level before adding Constitution. The rounds need not be consecutive. While the ability is active, each ally within 5 feet gains the specialist's current tower shield AC bonus as a shield {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g} to {g|Encyclopedia:Armor_Class}AC{/g}, including the shield's enhancement bonus.

While adjacent to a tower shield specialist using I Am Your Shield, this character gains the specialist's current tower shield AC bonus as a shield {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g} to {g|Encyclopedia:Armor_Class}AC{/g}, including the shield's enhancement bonus.

At 2nd level, a two-handed fighter gains a +1 bonus to CMB and CMD on sunder and disarm attempts. This bonus increases by +1 for every 4 additional fighter levels, to a maximum of +5 at 18th level. Each rank of Strong Grip also grants a +1 inherent {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g} to {g|Encyclopedia:Strength}Strength{/g}.

At 2nd level, a dragonheir scion gains a +2 {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g} on {g|Encyclopedia:Persuasion}Persuasion{/g} skill checks made to intimidate. This bonus increases by an additional 2 every 4 fighter levels thereafter, to +4 at 6th level, +6 at 10th level, +8 at 14th level, and a maximum of +10 at 18th level.

At 20th level, a hunter becomes a master hunter. He gains the ability to receive the animal focus benefits any amount of times per day. In addition, while the hunter or his animal companion is under the effect of an Animal Focus, that creature gains a +2 dodge {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g} to {g|Encyclopedia:Armor_Class}AC{/g} and a +2 bonus to {g|Encyclopedia:Base_Attack_Bonus}Base Attack Bonus{/g}.

While under the effect of an Animal Focus, this creature gains a +2 dodge {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g} to {g|Encyclopedia:Armor_Class}AC{/g} and a +2 bonus to {g|Encyclopedia:Base_Attack_Bonus}Base Attack Bonus{/g}.

At 2nd level, a hunter chooses either Precise Shot or Outflank as a bonus {g|Encyclopedia:Feat}feat{/g}. She does not need to meet the prerequisites for this feat. At 5th level, she gains Precise Companion again and chooses the other feat.

At 13th level, through constant care and training, the hunter's animal companion has become a mighty beast. The companion's natural armor increases by +2, and it gains +2 {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonuses{/g} to {g|Encyclopedia:Strength}Strength{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:Dexterity}Dexterity{/g}, and {g|Encyclopedia:Constitution}Constitution{/g}.

At 20th level, a divine hound can use Judgment any number of times per day. In addition, while the divine hound or animal companion is under the effect of a Judgment, that creature gains a +2 dodge {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g} to {g|Encyclopedia:Armor_Class}AC{/g} and a +2 bonus to {g|Encyclopedia:Base_Attack_Bonus}Base Attack Bonus{/g}.

While under the effect of a Judgment, this creature gains a +2 dodge {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g} to {g|Encyclopedia:Armor_Class}AC{/g} and a +2 bonus to {g|Encyclopedia:Base_Attack_Bonus}Base Attack Bonus{/g}.

At 10th level, when a tandem executioner and animal companion have both made a weapon attack against the same enemy, each adds 1d6 {g|Encyclopedia:Sneak_Attack}sneak attack{/g} precision damage to weapon attacks against that enemy. The effect ends if either partner attacks a different enemy and resets when combat ends.
The tandem executioner and animal companion are attacking this enemy together. Their weapon attacks against it deal 1d6 additional sneak attack precision damage.

At 10th level, an inquisitor gains 2 additional uses of {g|Encyclopedia:Judgment}Judgement{/g} per day and a +4 insight {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g} to {g|Encyclopedia:Wisdom}Wisdom{/g}. Inquisitor archetypes that give up Judgement do not gain Experienced Judgement.

At 20th level, an inquisitor can call true judgment down upon a foe during combat. Whenever an inquisitor uses her judgment ability, the inquisitor can invoke true judgment on a foe as a {g|Encyclopedia:Swift_Action}swift action{/g}. Once declared, the inquisitor can make a single {g|Encyclopedia:Attack}attack{/g}. If the attack hits, it deals {g|Encyclopedia:Damage}damage{/g} normally and the target must make a {g|Encyclopedia:Saving_Throw}Fortitude save{/g} or die. The {g|Encyclopedia:DC}DC{/g} of this save is equal to 10 + 1/2 the inquisitor's level + the inquisitor's {g|Encyclopedia:Wisdom}Wisdom{/g} modifier. Regardless of whether or not the save is made, the target creature is immune to the inquisitor's true judgment ability for 24 hours. In addition, the inquisitor can have up to four judgment effects active simultaneously.

When wearing light or no armor and not using a shield, a magus adds 1 point of {g|Encyclopedia:Intelligence}Intelligence{/g} bonus (if any) per magus class level as a dodge {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g} to {g|Encyclopedia:Armor_Class}Armor Class{/g}. If the magus is caught {g|Encyclopedia:Flat_Footed}flat-footed{/g} or otherwise denied the Dexterity bonus, the magus also loses this bonus.

At 20th level, a monk becomes a magical creature. The monk gains {g|Encyclopedia:Damage_Reduction}damage reduction{/g} 10/chaotic, which allows the monk to ignore the first 10 points of damage from any attack made by a nonchaotic weapon or by any natural attack made by a creature that does not have similar damage reduction. In addition, each hit with an {g|Encyclopedia:Unarmed_Attack}unarmed attack{/g} deals an additional 1d10 force damage.

At 7th level, a quarterstaff master gains a +1 weapon training {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g} on {g|Encyclopedia:Attack}attack{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:Damage}damage{/g} rolls with quarterstaves. This bonus increases by +1 at 10th, 13th, and 16th levels, to a maximum of +4.

The character can react to danger before her senses would normally allow her to do so. She cannot be caught {g|Encyclopedia:Flat_Footed}flat-footed{/g}, nor does she lose her Dexterity bonus to {g|Encyclopedia:Armor_Class}AC{/g} if the attacker is invisible. She still loses her Dexterity bonus to AC if immobilized. A character with this ability can still lose her Dexterity bonus to AC if an opponent successfully uses the feint action against her. If the character already has Uncanny Dodge from a different class, she automatically gains Improved Uncanny Dodge instead.

At 3rd level, a student of stone gains a +1 {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g} on attack and damage rolls, a +1 bonus on Trip and Bull Rush combat maneuver checks, and a +1 bonus to combat maneuver defense against Trip and Bull Rush. At 9th level, unarmed hits deal an additional 1d6 bludgeoning damage. At 15th level, the student of stone gains +4 inherent bonuses to {g|Encyclopedia:Strength}Strength{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:Constitution}Constitution{/g}.

At 9th level, Strength of Stone causes every {g|Encyclopedia:Unarmed_Attack}unarmed hit{/g} to deal an additional 1d6 bludgeoning damage. This damage does not apply to manufactured weapons or natural attacks.
At 15th level, Strength of Stone grants +4 inherent bonuses to {g|Encyclopedia:Strength}Strength{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:Constitution}Constitution{/g}.
At 7th level, a traditional monk's unarmed attack damage dice are treated as one size category larger.
At 11th level, Mastering the fundamentals grants the traditional monk a +2 dodge {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g} to {g|Encyclopedia:Armor_Class}Armor Class{/g}.

At 15th level, Mastering the fundamentals grants the traditional monk one additional attack at the monk's highest attack bonus while using {g|Encyclopedia:Flurry_Of_Blows}Flurry of Blows{/g}. The extra attack follows Flurry of Blows' normal armor, shield, and weapon restrictions.

At 15th level, a zen archer treats the damage dice of unarmed strikes as one size category larger. Ki Arrows carries this improvement over to longbows, composite longbows, shortbows, and composite shortbows.

At 20th level, a zen archer becomes one with the arrow. While using {g|Encyclopedia:Flurry_Of_Blows}Flurry of Blows{/g} with a longbow, composite longbow, shortbow, or composite shortbow, the zen archer makes one additional attack at the highest attack bonus. In addition, the critical threat range of all such bows increases by 1. This feature replaces Ki Power: Perfect Self.
At 1st level, a paladin gains {g|Encyclopedia:Weapon_Focus}Weapon Focus{/g} with the favored weapon of the paladin's chosen deity.

Beginning at 2nd level, a paladin can {g|Encyclopedia:Healing}heal{/g} wounds (her own or those of others) by touch. Each day she can use this ability a number of times equal to her paladin level plus her {g|Encyclopedia:Charisma}Charisma{/g} modifier. With one use of this ability, a paladin can heal {g|Encyclopedia:Dice}1d6{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:HP}hit points{/g} of damage for every two paladin levels she possesses. Using this ability is a {g|Encyclopedia:Standard_Actions}standard action{/g}, unless the paladin targets herself, in which case it is a {g|Encyclopedia:Swift_Action}swift action{/g}.
Alternatively, a paladin can use this healing power to deal {g|Encyclopedia:Damage}damage{/g} to undead creatures, dealing 1d6 points of damage for every two levels the paladin possesses. Using lay on hands in this way requires a successful melee {g|Encyclopedia:TouchAttack}touch attack{/g} and doesn't provoke an {g|Encyclopedia:Attack_Of_Opportunity}attack of opportunity{/g}. Undead do not receive a {g|Encyclopedia:Saving_Throw}saving throw{/g} against this damage.

Beginning at 2nd level, a paladin can {g|Encyclopedia:Healing}heal{/g} wounds (her own or those of others) by touch. Each day she can use this ability a number of times equal to her paladin level plus her {g|Encyclopedia:Charisma}Charisma{/g} modifier. With one use of this ability, a paladin can heal {g|Encyclopedia:Dice}1d6{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:HP}hit points{/g} of damage for every two paladin levels she possesses. Using this ability is a {g|Encyclopedia:Standard_Actions}standard action{/g}, unless the paladin targets herself or her divine troth, in which case it is a {g|Encyclopedia:Swift_Action}swift action{/g}. Despite the name of this ability, a paladin only needs one free hand to use this ability.
Alternatively, a paladin can use this healing power to deal {g|Encyclopedia:Damage}damage{/g} to undead creatures, dealing 1d6 points of damage for every two levels the paladin possesses. Using lay on hands in this way requires a successful melee {g|Encyclopedia:TouchAttack}touch attack{/g} and doesn't provoke an {g|Encyclopedia:Attack_Of_Opportunity}attack of opportunity{/g}. Undead do not receive a {g|Encyclopedia:Saving_Throw}saving throw{/g} against this damage.

At 2nd level, a tortured crusader can {g|Encyclopedia:Healing}heal{/g} her wounds by touch as a {g|Encyclopedia:Swift_Action}swift action{/g}. Each day she can use this ability a number of times equal to her paladin level plus her {g|Encyclopedia:Charisma}Charisma{/g} modifier. With one use of this ability, a tortured crusader can heal {g|Encyclopedia:Dice}1d6{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:HP}hit points{/g} of {g|Encyclopedia:Damage}damage{/g} for every two paladin levels she possesses.
At 8th level, this healing increases to 1d8 hit points of damage for every two paladin levels.
At 15th level, this healing is maximized as though affected by the {g|FeatureMaximizeSpell}Maximize Spell{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:Feat}feat{/g}.

At 4th level, the warrior of the holy light gains one additional use of her lay on hands ability per day. The character can react to danger before her senses would normally allow her to do so. She still loses her Dexterity bonus to AC if immobilized. A character with this ability can still lose her Dexterity bonus to AC if an opponent successfully uses the feint action against her. If the character already has Uncanny Dodge from a different class, she automatically gains Improved Uncanny Dodge instead.

At 20th level, the slayer becomes a master at capturing or killing his studied targets. As a {g|Encyclopedia:Standard_Actions}standard action{/g}, he can make a single {g|Encyclopedia:Attack}attack{/g} against a studied target at his full attack {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g}. If the attack succeeds, the target takes {g|Encyclopedia:Damage}damage{/g} normally and must succeed at a {g|Encyclopedia:Saving_Throw}Fortitude saving throw{/g} or die. Whether or not the target succeeds, it cannot be targeted by this ability again (by any slayer) for 24 hours. In addition, the slayer gains an insight bonus on attack rolls against his own studied targets equal to half his Intelligence modifier, rounded down (minimum +0).

A paladin who chooses the Combat Training path gains a bonus combat {g|Encyclopedia:Feat}feat{/g} at 3rd, 9th, and 15th levels in the same way a fighter does. The paladin must meet the selected feat's prerequisites.
At 3rd level, a paladin chooses between continuing the normal Mercy progression or replacing it with Combat Training. This choice determines the features gained at later paladin levels.
The paladin follows the normal Mercy progression, choosing a Mercy at 3rd level and every 3 paladin levels thereafter, through 18th level.

The paladin gives up the entire Mercy progression and instead selects a bonus combat {g|Encyclopedia:Feat}feat{/g} at 3rd, 9th, and 15th levels. These selections use the fighter's combat feat list, and the paladin must meet each feat's prerequisites.

You gain one additional witch hex for which you meet the prerequisites. You can select this feat multiple times; each time, you gain another hex.

You gain one additional shaman hex for which you meet the prerequisites. The hex must come from your spirit rather than a wandering spirit. You can select this feat multiple times; each time, you gain another hex.
You gain one additional oracle revelation for which you meet the prerequisites. You can select this feat multiple times; each time, you gain another revelation.
At 4th level, a cavalier learns to train mounts with speed and unsurpassed expertise. Beast Riders, Disciples of the Pike, and Knights of the Wall trade away this class feature.

Prerequisites: 6 ranks in Mobility and an animal companion.
You blend horsemanship skills from disparate traditions into a seamless mounted combat technique. Use your character level instead of your effective class level to determine the powers and abilities of your mount.

Prerequisites: Erastil and Weapon Focus (Longbow).
Your deity grants you prowess with a bow that far exceeds your physical capabilities. You can use your Wisdom modifier instead of your Dexterity modifier on ranged attack rolls made with longbows or shortbows, including composite bows.

Prerequisites: Channel Energy and proficiency with your deity's favored weapon.
With your deity's favored weapon, you can use your Wisdom modifier instead of your Strength or Dexterity modifier on attack rolls.

Prerequisites: Strength 13 and Power Attack.
When you successfully demoralize an opponent within melee reach, you can spend your swift action to make one melee attack against that opponent. Use the Hurtful toggle to control this response. If the attack misses, the shaken effect applied by that demoralize ends.

You can take advantage of a distracted foe. Dirty Fighting counts as Dexterity 13, Intelligence 13, Combat Expertise, and Improved Unarmed Strike for combat-maneuver feat prerequisites and grants access to the standard combat-maneuver actions. A maneuver made without its corresponding improved feat takes a -4 penalty, reduced to -2 while the target is flanked. If you possess the corresponding improved feat, a maneuver against a flanked target instead gains a +2 bonus.

Prerequisite: Witch level 10.
When you use a single-target witch hex that is not a major or grand hex, you can use the same hex again against a different creature as a free action before the end of the round. Use the Split Hex toggle to control this option.
Split Hex must target a different creature.

Prerequisites: Shield Focus; base attack bonus +3 or Fighter level 1; proficiency with light, heavy, or tower shields.
You can use a two-handed polearm or spear sized appropriately for you while also using a light, heavy, or tower shield with which you are proficient. The shield's armor check penalty applies to attacks made with the weapon, and the weapon is treated as one-handed while braced.

You are skilled at defending yourself while dual-wielding. When wielding a double weapon or two weapons (not including natural weapons or unarmed strikes), you gain a +1 dodge bonus to Armor Class. While fighting defensively, this dodge bonus increases to +2.
Prerequisites: Dexterity 15 and Two-Weapon Fighting.

Your fiendish traits take the form of protective scaly skin. You gain a +2 natural armor bonus to Armor Class.
Prerequisite: Tiefling.

Your unarmed strikes deal at least 1d8 base damage for a Medium creature, increasing to 1d10 at character level 10. If you have Monk levels, add 4 to your effective Monk level when determining your unarmed strike damage dice. This feat never reduces stronger unarmed strike damage dice.
Prerequisites: Improved Unarmed Strike and character level 3.

Prerequisites: Dexterity 13, Weapon Finesse, Mobility 2, scimitar proficiency.
When wielding a scimitar one-handed with your other hand free, you can use your Dexterity modifier instead of your Strength modifier on melee attack and damage rolls.
As a full-round action that provokes attacks of opportunity, you can spend 1 point from your arcane reservoir to replace one prepared spell with another spell of the same level from your spellbook.

Prerequisite: Bloodrage.
You can cast spells from any class while bloodraging. Once you gain Greater Bloodrage, spells cast during it gain +1 to their saving throw DC.

Prerequisites: Channel Energy, Flurry of Blows, and Weapon Focus with your deity's favored melee weapon.
You can use your deity's favored melee weapon as a monk weapon when performing a flurry of blows.

A rime spell causes creatures damaged by its cold damage to become entangled for a number of rounds equal to the spell's original level. This feat only affects spells with the cold descriptor.

The clinging frost of a rime spell has entangled this creature.

You can use your Charisma modifier instead of Strength or Dexterity on attack and damage rolls with starknives.

Prerequisites: Weapon Focus with the selected monk weapon; Monk level 1 or base attack bonus +1.
Select a monk weapon as the focus of your ascetic discipline. This choice is used by Ascetic Form and Ascetic Strike.

Prerequisites: Ascetic Style with the selected weapon; Monk level 5 or base attack bonus +5.
You can use the selected monk weapon with Flurry of Blows.

The selected weapon uses your unarmed strike damage as a monk of your character level minus 4 whenever that damage is higher than the weapon's normal damage.

This feat can only be selected at 1st character level. Whenever you receive magical healing, you regain 2 additional hit points per die rolled. You gain a +2 bonus on saving throws against death effects, but cold iron weapons deal 1 additional point of damage to you.

Prerequisites: Combat Reflexes and Improved Unarmed Strike.
Whenever an adjacent enemy falls prone, you can make an attack of opportunity against that enemy with an unarmed strike.

Prerequisites: Intelligence 13 and the ability to cast 1st-level paladin spells.
Choose one spell of each spell level from 1st through 4th from the bard, cleric, or inquisitor spell lists. Add those spells to your paladin spell list and paladin spellbook.

Prerequisites: Strength 13 and base attack bonus +1.
When making ranged attack rolls with throwing axes, darts, javelins, or shuriken, you use your Strength modifier instead of Dexterity whenever it is higher. This does not affect bombs, kinetic blasts, rays, or projectile weapons.

Prerequisites: Strength 15, base attack bonus +6, Mighty Hurling, and Power Attack.
While Power Attack is active, its attack penalty and damage bonus also apply to throwing axes, darts, javelins, and shuriken. These attacks use one-handed Power Attack scaling, and off-hand attacks receive half the normal damage bonus.

Prerequisites: Dexterity 13, base attack bonus +1, Weapon Finesse, and Weapon Focus with the selected weapon.
Choose one type of one-handed slashing or piercing melee weapon. When wielding it in one hand, you can use Weapon Finesse with it and it counts as light when calculating two-weapon fighting penalties. Mythic Weapon Finesse also applies to the selected weapon. This does not change its proficiency, damage dice, fighter weapon group, reach, or number of hands required. You can select this feat multiple times for different weapons.

You unleash an insulting tirade at your enemies. Make an Intimidate check to demoralize every enemy within 30 feet. Each enemy successfully demoralized also takes 1d10 points of fire damage and must succeed at a Reflex save or catch fire. Spell resistance protects against the fire effects but not the demoralization.

The creature takes 1d6 points of fire damage immediately and again each round. At the start of each new round it attempts a DC 15 Reflex save; success extinguishes the flames. The fire burns for no more than 10 rounds.

You create a 10-foot emanation of harmonized magic for 1 round per caster level. When casting this spell, choose Extend or Reach. Every arcane spell cast within the emanation gains a +1 enhancement bonus to its saving throw DC and the chosen metamagic effect without increasing its spell level or casting time.
Arcane spells cast within the emanation gain a +1 enhancement bonus to their saving throw DC and the selected free metamagic effect.

This spell fills a 10-foot-radius burst with brilliant radiance. Every creature in the area must attempt a Reflex save. A creature that succeeds is dazzled for 1d4 rounds; one that fails is blinded for 1d4 rounds. Evil creatures also take 1d4 points of damage per caster level, to a maximum of 5d4, regardless of the saving throw result.
The creature is blinded by the brilliant radiance.
The creature is dazzled by the brilliant radiance.

For 1 minute per caster level, an invisible blade tutor guides your attacks. The spell reduces voluntary penalties on your melee attack rolls from Power Attack, Piranha Strike, Combat Expertise, Fighting Defensively, Spell Combat, and charging by 1, plus 1 for every 5 caster levels. It cannot reduce a penalty below 0.

Each time you reduce an enemy to 0 or fewer hit points with a melee attack, you gain a cumulative +1 luck bonus on melee attack rolls, melee weapon damage rolls, Strength checks, and Athletics checks, as well as DR 2/—. These benefits can accumulate up to five times, for a maximum +5 luck bonus and DR 10/—. An enemy whose Hit Dice are more than 4 lower than your character level does not grant a stack. All stacks end when the spell expires.
Character traits are small abilities reflecting a character's upbringing, training, or personality. At character creation, choose two different traits.
You have studied the workings of anatomy and know where to aim your blows to strike vital organs. You gain a +1 bonus on all attack rolls made to confirm critical hits.
You have worn armor for as long as you can remember and know how to move naturally in it. Reduce your armor check penalty by 1.

You were bullied often as a child, but never quite developed an offensive response. Instead, you became adept at anticipating sudden attacks and reacting quickly to danger. You gain a +2 trait bonus on initiative checks.
Growing up in a poor district or under harsh conditions, you were forced to subsist on food and water from doubtful sources. You gain a +1 trait bonus on Fortitude saving throws.
You gain a +1 trait bonus on attack rolls made for attacks of opportunity with unarmed strikes.
You gain a +2 trait bonus on saving throws against fear effects.
You gain a +1 trait bonus on Reflex saving throws.
You gain a +1 trait bonus on weapon damage rolls against enemies you are flanking.
You gain a +1 trait bonus on attack rolls made for attacks of opportunity with weapons from the light blades or heavy blades weapon groups.
When you confirm a critical hit with a weapon, it deals additional damage equal to that weapon's critical multiplier. This additional damage is not multiplied by the critical hit.
The critical multiplier of your claw attacks increases by 1.

When two-weapon fighting with a shield in your off hand, the shield counts as a light weapon for determining two-weapon fighting penalties. You gain a +1 trait bonus on damage rolls made with shield bashes.
You gain a +2 trait bonus on saving throws against charm and compulsion effects.
You gain a +1 trait bonus on Knowledge (World) and Lore (Nature) checks. Choose one of these skills to become a class skill.
Devotee of the Green — Class Skill
You gain a +1 trait bonus on Persuasion checks, and Persuasion becomes a class skill for you.
You gain a +1 trait bonus on saving throws against divine spells while you have no levels in a divine spellcasting class.
You gain a +1 trait bonus on Will saving throws.
The saving throw DC of your Channel Energy abilities increases by 1.
You gain a +1 trait bonus on Knowledge (World) and Knowledge (Arcana) checks. Choose one of these skills to become a class skill.
Scholar of the Great Beyond — Class Skill
You gain a +1 trait bonus on Use Magic Device checks, and Use Magic Device becomes a class skill for you.
You gain a +2 trait bonus on concentration checks.
You gain a +2 trait bonus on saving throws against illusion spells.
You gain a +1 trait bonus on Knowledge (Arcana) and Use Magic Device checks. Choose one of these skills to become a class skill.
You gain a +1 trait bonus on Persuasion checks, and Persuasion becomes a class skill for you.
You gain a +1 trait bonus on Trickery checks, and Trickery becomes a class skill for you.
You gain a +1 trait bonus on Persuasion checks, and Persuasion becomes a class skill for you.
You were raised by members of a race other than your own. Select one racial trait belonging to any other playable race.

For 1 minute per caster level, each club or quarterstaff you wield gains a +1 enhancement bonus on attack and damage rolls and deals damage as though it were two size categories larger. Both ends of a quarterstaff receive the benefits. This affects magical and nonmagical weapons alike.
You gain a +1 trait bonus on Persuasion checks and a +1 trait bonus on combat maneuver checks.
You gain a +1 trait bonus on saving throws against arcane spells.

You gain a +1 trait bonus on weapon damage rolls with bastard swords, battleaxes, greataxes, greatswords, handaxes, light hammers, shortbows, longbows, longswords, shortswords, throwing axes, and warhammers.
You gain a +2 trait bonus on initiative checks.
You gain a +1 trait bonus on Fortitude saving throws.
You gain a +2 trait bonus on Will saving throws against charm, compulsion, and fear effects produced by non-elven humanoids.
You gain a +1 trait bonus on rolls to confirm critical hits.
You gain a +2 trait bonus on Mobility checks and a +1 trait bonus on Reflex saving throws.
You gain a +1 trait bonus on Lore (Nature) checks and a +1 trait bonus on saving throws against fear effects.
While underground, you gain a +2 bonus on initiative checks. Confirmed critical hits with weapons also deal 1 additional point of damage before the critical multiplier is applied.

You gain a +1 trait bonus on weapon damage rolls against constructs, earth elementals, gargoyles, golems, and creatures primarily made from stone, crystal, earth, or metal. Knowledge (World) becomes a class skill for you.
Once per day, after you fail a saving throw against an emotion effect, you gain 1d6 temporary hit points for 1 minute.
Your caster level is treated as 1 higher when casting illusion spells.
You gain a +1 trait bonus on Mobility checks and a +1 trait bonus on initiative checks.
You gain a +1 trait bonus on Will saving throws while a friendly animal is within 30 feet.
You gain a +1 trait bonus on Persuasion and Knowledge (World) checks. Choose one of these skills to become a class skill for you.
Choose either Athletics or combat maneuvers. The selected option uses Dexterity instead of Strength.
You gain a +1 trait bonus on Stealth checks and a +2 trait bonus on Persuasion checks made to demoralize enemies.
You gain a +2 trait bonus on initiative checks.
You gain a +1 trait bonus on saving throws against arcane spells.
You gain a +2 trait bonus on saving throws against spells and abilities produced by elves.
Once per rage or bloodrage, confirming a critical hit restores 1 round of the active rage resource.
You gain a +1 trait bonus on attack rolls against opponents you have damaged within the last 24 hours.
Your bite and gore attacks deal damage as though they were one size category larger.
You gain a +1 trait bonus on Persuasion and Perception checks.
Whenever you score a critical threat, add damage equal to the weapon's critical multiplier. This additional damage is not multiplied if the critical hit confirms.
Your caster level is treated as 1 higher when casting spells with the good descriptor.
While at or below half your maximum hit points, you gain a +1 trait bonus on attack rolls against evil creatures.
You gain a +2 trait bonus on rolls to confirm critical hits with shortbows and longbows.
You gain a +1 trait bonus on saving throws against charm and compulsion effects.
You gain a +2 trait bonus on saving throws against disease effects.
Your caster level is treated as 1 higher when casting spells with the evil descriptor.
You gain a +2 trait bonus to Armor Class against attacks of opportunity from enemies who are flanked or cannot see you.
You deal 2 additional points of melee weapon damage against enemies that cannot see you.
During a surprise round and before your first action, you apply half your Dexterity bonus to Armor Class even while flat-footed.
You gain a +2 trait bonus on saving throws against curse and hex effects.
While you are conscious, you gain a +1 trait bonus on saving throws against new mind-affecting effects. Allies within 10 feet gain a +1 morale bonus on those saving throws.
You gain a +1 trait bonus on Knowledge (World) and Lore (Religion) checks. Choose one of these skills to become a class skill for you.
Acknowledged Scion — Choose a Class Skill
You gain a +1 trait bonus on attack and weapon damage rolls against undead.
Choose two of Knowledge (Arcana), Knowledge (World), Lore (Nature), and Lore (Religion). You gain a +1 trait bonus on both selected skills and make one of them a class skill.
Whenever you are under the effect of a luck bonus of any kind, that bonus increases by 1.
You use your Intelligence modifier instead of your Charisma modifier for Use Magic Device checks.
You use your Intelligence modifier instead of your Charisma modifier for Persuasion checks made to intimidate.
Choose one spellcasting class in which you have at least 1 level, then choose one cantrip from another class's spell list. You add that cantrip to the chosen class's spells known.
Select one spell. Your caster level for that spell increases by 1.
Additional backgrounds tied to the Worldwound and the Fifth Crusade.
Lore (Nature) and Mobility become class skills and gain a +1 trait bonus. You gain a +1 trait bonus on weapon damage rolls against demons.
You gain a +2 trait bonus to initiative and saving throws against fear effects.
Lore (Religion) and Use Magic Device become class skills and gain a +1 trait bonus. You gain a +2 trait bonus on saving throws against compulsion effects and abilities used by demons.
Perception and Persuasion become class skills and gain a +1 trait bonus. Choose proficiency with light armor or light shields.
Knowledge (Arcana) and Use Magic Device become class skills and gain a +1 trait bonus. You gain a +1 trait bonus on weapon attack and damage rolls against constructs.
Lore (Religion) becomes a class skill and gains a +1 trait bonus. You gain proficiency with your deity's favored weapon.
Knowledge (World) and Persuasion become class skills and gain a +1 trait bonus. Your personal carrying capacity increases by 50 pounds.
Perception and Lore (Nature) become class skills and gain a +1 trait bonus. You gain a +4 bonus to initiative when you begin combat surprised.
Select a sorcerer bloodline. You gain its 1st-level bloodline power, using your character level minus 2 as your effective sorcerer level.
Your inherited bloodline deepens. Select one eligible 3rd- or 9th-level power from the bloodline chosen with Eldritch Heritage.

Your inherited bloodline reaches its height. Gain an eligible 15th-level power from the bloodline chosen with Eldritch Heritage, and improve the effective level of your inherited powers. At character level 20, you also gain that bloodline's capstone power.

Select one natural weapon for which you have Weapon Focus. You can use that natural weapon with feats, Monk abilities, and style effects that normally require unarmed strikes. It also gains iterative attacks from a high base attack bonus.
Choose another race. You count as both Human and the chosen race for prerequisites and may select its racial character traits.
You may use Intelligence instead of Dexterity to meet the prerequisites of combat feats.

When a manufactured ranged weapon attack targets you while you are not flat-footed, you may spend an attack of opportunity and make a melee attack roll. If your result equals or exceeds the incoming attack roll, the ranged attack misses.
Your cunning guides your senses. You use your Intelligence modifier instead of your Wisdom modifier on Perception checks.
Your sense of self remains steady in either form. You gain a +2 trait bonus on saving throws against polymorph, charm, and compulsion effects.
You are practiced at concealing your nature and intentions. You gain a +1 trait bonus on Stealth and Persuasion checks, and choose one of these skills to become a class skill.
You gain a +2 trait bonus on initiative checks. During a surprise round, you also gain a +1 trait bonus on attack rolls against surprised creatures.
Your keen mind is more pronounced than your natural charm. You gain +2 Intelligence and lose the Kitsune's +2 racial Charisma bonus.
You gain 1 additional skill point at 1st level and whenever you gain a character level. This replaces Agile and Kitsune Magic.
You can activate or dismiss your Kitsune Change Shape ability as a move action instead of a standard action. This replaces Kitsune Magic.
Choose two ability scores. Your animal companion or bonded mount gains a +2 racial bonus to each chosen ability score and 4 additional hit points. This replaces the human bonus feat.
You gain a +1 racial bonus on Perception checks and a +2 racial bonus on saving throws against spells and abilities used by fey. This replaces Skilled.
At 1st, 8th, and 16th character level, you gain Skill Focus in a skill of your choice. This replaces the human bonus feat.
You gain a +1 racial bonus on all saving throws and concentration checks. This replaces the human bonus feat.
You gain proficiency with two martial or exotic weapons of your choice. This replaces the human bonus feat.
You gain a +2 racial bonus on caster level checks made to overcome spell resistance. This replaces the human bonus feat.
You gain a +2 racial bonus on Persuasion, Perception, and Stealth checks. This replaces Skilled.
You gain a +1 racial bonus to combat maneuver checks and combat maneuver defense, but take a -2 racial penalty on Stealth checks. This replaces Skilled.
You gain a +2 racial bonus on Trickery and Stealth checks and roll twice on saving throws against disease, taking the better result. This replaces Skilled.
You gain a +2 racial bonus on Stealth and Lore (Nature) checks, and both skills become class skills. This replaces Skilled.
You gain a +2 racial bonus on initiative and Mobility checks, and your base movement speed increases by 5 feet. This replaces Keen Senses and Elven Weapon Familiarity.
The saving throw DC of your enchantment spells increases by 1. This replaces Elven Immunities.
You gain spell resistance equal to 5 + your character level, but your caster level for all spells is reduced by 2. This replaces Hardy.
You gain a +2 racial bonus on combat maneuver checks made to bull rush or overrun an opponent. This replaces Stability.
Treat your caster level as 1 higher when casting spells with the fire descriptor.

You gain a +2 racial bonus on saving throws against fear and emotion effects. Once per day, the first natural 1 you roll on a d20 is automatically rerolled, keeping the better result. This replaces Defensive Training and Hatred.
The saving throw DC of your necromancy spells increases by 1. This replaces Gnome Magic.
As a standard action, you can jinx one enemy within close range. The target takes a -1 penalty on all saving throws for 3 rounds. This replaces Halfling Luck.
You gain a +1 racial bonus on critical confirmation rolls against creatures larger than you. This replaces Keen Senses.
Choose the martial weapon proficiency package or proficiency with one exotic weapon. This replaces Adaptability.
You gain a +2 racial bonus on Will saving throws.
You gain a +1 luck bonus on all saving throws. This replaces Orc Ferocity.
You gain a 1d4 bite attack. This replaces Orc Ferocity.
You gain Endurance as a bonus feat. This replaces Intimidating.
Treat your caster level as 1 higher for spells with the good descriptor and for spells of light, radiance, and sunlight. This replaces your ancestry's racial skill bonuses and spell-like ability.
You gain resistance 5 against negative energy damage and a +2 racial bonus on saving throws against death effects and negative levels. This replaces Celestial Resistance.
You gain a +1 insight bonus on attack rolls and to Armor Class against evil outsiders. This replaces Celestial Resistance and your ancestry's racial skill bonuses.
Choose either a 1d6 bite attack or two 1d4 claw attacks. This replaces your ancestry's racial spell-like ability.
You gain a +10-foot racial bonus to movement speed while charging. This replaces your ancestry's racial skill bonuses.
You are immune to the dazzled condition. This replaces Resist Level Drain.
You gain a 1d6 bite attack. This replaces Undead Resistance.
Whenever you take acid damage, you recover 2 hit points. This replaces Acid Affinity.
Treat your caster level as 1 higher for acid spells and spells associated with earth, stone, or rock. This replaces Acid Affinity.
Choose an alternate racial heritage or retain your standard racial abilities. Choosing an alternate heritage opens another page when a compatible additional heritage remains available.
Retain the standard racial abilities for your chosen race and ancestry.
Choose another compatible racial heritage that replaces different racial abilities, or select No Additional Heritage.

While raging, you gain a +2 morale bonus on saving throws against hostile spells, spell-like abilities, and supernatural abilities used by enemies. This bonus increases by +1 for every four effective rage-power levels.
While raging, you gain +1 weapon damage against creatures that possess spells or spell-like abilities. This bonus increases by +1 for every four effective rage-power levels. Requires Superstition.

Once per rage, when you fail a saving throw against hostile magic, you immediately reroll it and keep the better result. If the second result succeeds, you gain temporary hit points equal to the effect's caster level for 1 minute. Requires Superstition.

As a free action while raging, empower your next combat maneuver check or combat maneuver defense check with a bonus equal to your effective rage-power level. You can use Strength Surge once per rage at level 8, twice per rage at level 12, and three times per rage at level 16.
Your next combat maneuver check or combat maneuver defense check gains a bonus equal to your effective rage-power level.
Strength Surge can only be prepared while raging, and only one surge can be prepared at a time.
Choose acid, cold, electricity, or fire. While raging, every weapon and natural attack deals an additional 1d6 damage of the chosen energy type.

Choose an Elemental Rage you possess. When you confirm a critical hit while raging, that attack deals an additional 1d6 damage of the chosen energy type for each point of the weapon's critical multiplier beyond ×1.

While raging, your melee attacks gain the ghost touch property and you gain a +3 morale bonus to touch Armor Class. The touch Armor Class bonus increases to +4 at effective rage-power level 8 and by +1 every four levels thereafter.
While you rage, your animal companion or bonded mount gains the attack, weapon damage, and Will saving throw bonuses of your rage while it remains mounted by or adjacent to you.
While you rage, your animal companion or bonded mount shares every rage power you possess for the duration of the rage. Requires Ferocious Mount.

While you rage and your companion remains mounted by or adjacent to you, its natural attacks count as magic and it gains damage reduction/magic equal to half your effective rage-power level. Requires Ferocious Mount.

You can toggle Hamstring Strike on or off. When active, a successful sneak attack forgoes all sneak-attack dice. The target must succeed at a Fortitude save (DC 10 + half your rogue level + your Dexterity modifier) or fall prone and become unable to move for 1 round.
You are prone and unable to move.

You can toggle Armor Piercer on or off. When active, a successful sneak attack forgoes all sneak-attack dice and reduces the target's natural armor by 1 for each die forgone until the end of your next turn.
You gain proficiency with heavy armor. While wearing heavy armor, its armor check penalty is reduced by 1 for every 6 slayer levels you possess.
You retain your full movement speed while wearing heavy armor. Its maximum Dexterity bonus increases by 1 for every 6 slayer levels you possess. Requires Armored Marauder.

Your sickles and scythes deal damage as though they were one size category larger and gain a +1 increase to their critical threat range. The threat-range increase does not stack with other threat-range increases.
The penalty on your secondary natural attacks is reduced from −5 to −2.
Choose one natural attack you possess. That natural attack deals damage as though it were one size category larger.
When you charge while fighting with two claws and no manufactured weapons, you can make your full complement of claw attacks at the end of the charge.
Choose a thrown weapon for which you possess Weapon Focus. Ranged attacks with that weapon do not provoke attacks of opportunity.
After your first unarmed hit against a creature in a round, each subsequent consecutive unarmed hit against that creature deals an additional 1d6 points of bludgeoning damage.
Your second and every later consecutive unarmed hit against the same creature in a round deals an additional 2d6 points of bludgeoning damage.

While wielding a ranged weapon, you gain a +1 competence bonus on ranged attack rolls for each conscious ally within 30 feet who also has Volley Fire and is wielding a ranged weapon, to a maximum of +4. Solo Tactics allows nearby allies with ranged weapons to qualify for your bonus.
You use your Intelligence modifier for damage with bows and crossbows. This replaces any other ability-score modifier to weapon damage instead of stacking with it.

You gain the benefits of Combat Reflexes, using your Intelligence modifier instead of Dexterity to determine your additional attacks of opportunity. Tactical Reflexes counts as Combat Reflexes for prerequisites.
The selected hand must hold a valid weapon for this spell.

The selected weapon gains a +2 sacred bonus on weapon damage rolls. Whenever it confirms a critical hit, the target is shaken for 1 round. This is a mind-affecting fear effect. A ranged weapon bestows these effects on its ammunition.
You are shaken by a critical hit from a weapon affected by Weapon of Awe.

The target's armor gains a +1 enhancement bonus for every four caster levels, to a maximum of +5. A target without armor gains the same enhancement bonus to Armor Class. While the target is using Judgment or Smite, the target also gains damage reduction 5/evil.

As part of casting this spell, make a normal melee attack. If the attack hits, it deals an additional 1d4 points of force damage per caster level, to a maximum of 10d4. A successful Fortitude save halves this force damage. On a failed save, you also attempt a bull rush using your caster level in place of your normal attack bonus.

Choose anarchic, axiomatic, holy, or unholy and apply that weapon special ability to the selected melee weapon. The spell cannot apply a special ability the weapon already possesses. A Warpriest casting this spell on their own weapon receives double duration.

At 4th level, a shieldbearer gains the ability to enhance his shield with divine power as a swift action. This ability functions as sacred armor, except as follows. This power grants the shield a +1 enhancement bonus to Armor Class. The same enhancement bonus applies to attack and damage rolls made with its shield bash. For every 4 warpriest levels beyond 4th, this bonus increases by 1, to a maximum of +5 at 20th level.

At 2nd level, a warpriest can draw upon the power of his faith to {g|Encyclopedia:Healing}heal{/g} wounds or harm foes. He can also use this ability to quickly cast {g|Encyclopedia:Spell}spells{/g} that aid in his struggles. This ability can be used a number of times per day equal to his warpriest level + his {g|Encyclopedia:Wisdom}Wisdom{/g} modifier. By expending one use of this ability, a {g|Encyclopedia:Alignment}good{/g} warpriest (or one who worships a good deity) can touch a creature to heal it of {g|Encyclopedia:Dice}1d6{/g} points of damage, plus an additional 1d6 points of damage for every 3 warpriest levels he possesses above 2nd (to a maximum of 7d6 at 20th level). Using this ability is a {g|Encyclopedia:Standard_Actions}standard action{/g} (unless the warpriest targets himself, in which case it's a {g|Encyclopedia:Swift_Action}swift action{/g}). Alternatively, the warpriest can use this ability to harm an undead creature, dealing the same amount of {g|Encyclopedia:Damage}damage{/g} he would otherwise heal with a melee {g|Encyclopedia:TouchAttack}touch attack{/g}. Using fervor in this way is a standard action that provokes an {g|Encyclopedia:Attack_Of_Opportunity}attack of opportunity{/g}. Undead do not receive a {g|Encyclopedia:Saving_Throw}saving throw{/g} against this damage. This counts as positive energy.
An evil warpriest (or one who worships an evil deity) can use this ability to instead deal damage to living creatures with a melee touch attack and heal undead creatures with a touch. This counts as negative energy.
A neutral warpriest who worships a neutral deity (or one who is not devoted to a particular deity) uses this ability as a good warpriest if he chose to spontaneously cast cure spells or as an evil warpriest if he chose to spontaneously cast inflict spells.

At 4th level, a cult leader can try to fascinate all enemies in a 30-foot radius as a {g|Encyclopedia:Move_Action}move action{/g}. Enemies that fail a {g|Encyclopedia:Saving_Throw}Will saving throw{/g} with a {g|Encyclopedia:DC}DC{/g} of 10 + half the cult leader's warpriest level + his {g|Encyclopedia:Wisdom}Wisdom{/g} modifier are fascinated for a number of {g|Encyclopedia:Combat_Round}rounds{/g} equal to his Wisdom modifier. Using this ability consumes two uses of fervor.

An arcane enforcer possesses a reservoir of arcane energy used to fuel arcane exploits. The reservoir's maximum and every ability-score-based value of the arcane enforcer's arcane exploits use {g|Encyclopedia:Intelligence}Intelligence{/g}.

Arcane exploits duplicate magical effects by expending points from the arcane reservoir. Unless otherwise noted, an exploit's saving throw DC is 10 + half the user's class level + the user's governing exploit ability modifier. Arcanists use {g|Encyclopedia:Charisma}Charisma{/g}; Arcane Enforcers use {g|Encyclopedia:Intelligence}Intelligence{/g} for saving throw DCs and all other ability-score-based effects.

At 4th level, a champion of the faith can focus his powers against his chosen foes. As a {g|Encyclopedia:Swift_Action}swift action{/g}, the champion of the faith chooses one target within sight to smite. If this target is of his opposed {g|Encyclopedia:Alignment}alignment{/g}, the champion of the faith adds his {g|Encyclopedia:Wisdom}Wisdom{/g} bonus (if any) to his {g|Encyclopedia:Attack}attack rolls{/g} and adds his warpriest level to all {g|Encyclopedia:Damage}damage rolls{/g} made against the target of his smite. Smite attacks automatically bypass any {g|Encyclopedia:Damage_Reduction}DR{/g} the target possesses.
In addition, while smite is in effect, the champion of the faith gains a deflection {g|Encyclopedia:Bonus}bonus{/g} equal to his Wisdom modifier (if any) to his {g|Encyclopedia:Armor_Class}AC{/g} against attacks made by the target of the smite. If the smite targets a creature that's not of the champion of the faith's opposed alignment, the smite is wasted with no effect.
The smite effect remains until the target of the smite is dead or the next time the champion of the faith regains {g|Encyclopedia:Spell}spells{/g}. The champion of the faith can use this ability once per day, plus one additional time per day for every 4 levels beyond 4th (to a maximum of five times per day at 20th level). Using this ability consumes two uses of his fervor ability.
The hagbound gains a +1 bonus on attack rolls with claws and increases the critical threat range of claws by 1. These bonuses increase by 1 at 7th level and again at 11th level.

At 10th level, whenever a keen-eyed adventurer casts a {g|Encyclopedia:Spell}spell{/g} that requires a ranged {g|Encyclopedia:TouchAttack}touch attack{/g}, that spell deals additional {g|Encyclopedia:Damage}damage{/g} equal to her {g|Encyclopedia:Intelligence}Intelligence{/g} modifier. This ability replaces the witch's 10th-level hex.
You can use hexes and major hexes as swift actions. Grand hexes are excluded.

Select one eligible single-target hex you know. While the Hex Strike toggle is active, after you hit an enemy with an unarmed strike or natural weapon, you can use the selected hex against that enemy as a swift action before the end of the round.
Hex Strike must target the creature you hit.

At 20th level, the witch's hexes and spells with the curse descriptor gain a +2 bonus to their saving throw DCs. The witch gains a +2 bonus on saving throws against hexes and effects with the curse descriptor. When a creature succeeds at its saving throw against one of the witch's hexes that cannot target the same creature more than once per day, the witch can target that creature with the same hex one additional time.

At 20th level, assuming or changing a shifter major form becomes a swift action. While a major form is active, the shifter gains a +10-foot bonus to movement speed and a +2 bonus on all saving throws.
A defender of the true world gains a +2 bonus on weapon attack and damage rolls against fey and evil outsiders.

At 3rd level, a defender of the true world's animal companion and summoned creatures gain a +1 bonus on weapon attack and damage rolls against fey and evil outsiders. This bonus increases by 1 at levels 8, 13, and 18.

At 4th level, a defender of the true world gains a +4 bonus on saving throws against the spell-like and supernatural abilities of fey and evil outsiders. Her natural weapons are treated as cold iron for the purpose of overcoming damage reduction, and she gains a +2 bonus on caster level checks to overcome the spell resistance of fey and evil outsiders.

At 20th level, a bard gains a +2 bonus on all skill checks and increases the saving throw DC of all bardic performances by 2. While a bardic performance is active, the bard gains a +4 bonus to Dexterity.
At 20th level, the alchemist's constant exposure to strange chemicals permanently increases Intelligence by 4.

The alchemist's cognatogen grants a +8 natural armor bonus to Armor Class and a +8 alchemical bonus to Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma. The alchemist takes a -2 penalty to Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution while the cognatogen persists.
Once per round, after you hit with a thrown weapon, you make a free secondary attack with that weapon at a -2 penalty against the nearest other enemy within 15 feet of the original target.

Your shield-bash damage dice increase by one size category. After your first successful shield bash each round, you gain a +2 bonus to Armor Class until the beginning of your next turn. This bonus stacks with all other Armor Class bonuses.
Equipped shields no longer impose arcane spell failure. A shield hand also counts as free for spellcasting abilities such as Spell Combat.
Your base speed is 20 feet, and you gain a +8 racial bonus on Athletics checks. This replaces the goblin's 30-foot base speed.
You gain a +2 racial bonus on Perception and Lore (Nature) checks. This replaces Stealthy and Keen Senses.

Dread Archers turn precision fire into terror. Their merciless reputation and painful shots break enemy morale, allowing them to inflict punishing damage on frightened foes. They train with every ranged weapon but forgo shields and heavy armor.
A Dread Archer is proficient with all simple and martial weapons and with light and medium armor.
The Dread Archer gains a +2 bonus on Persuasion checks made to demoralize enemies for each rank of this ability.

The Dread Archer gains a +1 bonus on attack and damage rolls with all ranged weapons. This bonus increases by 1 at levels 9, 13, and 17. Ranged Weapon Training counts as Weapon Training for all effects and prerequisites.
While Deadly Aim is active, the first enemy hit by one of the Dread Archer's ranged weapon attacks each round is subjected to a free demoralize attempt.
The Dread Archer deals 1d6 additional physical damage with all attacks against creatures that are shaken or under a fear effect. At level 16, this increases to 2d6.
The range of the Dread Archer's Dreadful Carnage increases to 50 feet.
